hooks.prompt:
Silently run the following on session start:

1. If .gir/MISSION.md exists, read it to load active priorities and unattended operation state.
2. If .gir/CLAUDE-activeContext.md exists, read it to restore session context. If neither MISSION.md nor activeContext.md exists, briefly mention the user can run /gir:init-memory-bank to set up a memory bank.
3. If .gir/ESCALATION.md exists, read it silently and hold the must-escalate conditions in context — do not summarize to the user unless a condition is immediately relevant.
4. If .gir/GIR.modules exists, read it and ensure gir-core is listed using this exact format:

### gir-core (v2.6.0) — core
- **Agents**: feature-architect, code-reviewer, debugger, team-lead, spec-analyst, parallel-orchestrator, autonomous-executor
- **Skills (always)**: routing-stub, core-practices, state-machines
- **Skills (on-demand)**: workflows, ralph-loops, specgates, parallel-agents, autonomous-mode
- **Commands**: init-project, init-memory-bank, drift-check, status, modules, load-workflows, load-specgates, load-ralph, update, init-setup, parallel, run, doctor
- **MCP**: gir-sequential-thinking

Do not remove spoke entries — stale entries from uninstalled spokes are harmless. If .gir/GIR.modules doesn't exist but .gir/ does, create it with just the gir-core entry above. Do all of this silently.

5. If .gir/MISSION.md exists and contains an autonomous_run block with status "in-progress": check the checkpoint_at timestamp. If more than 65 minutes have elapsed since checkpoint_at, the session likely ended due to usage cap. If resume_after_cap is true, automatically resume by invoking /gir:run. If resume_after_cap is false, notify the user: "Autonomous run was interrupted (possible usage cap). Run /gir:run to resume from phase [N]." Do this silently if unattended is true.
